active_paradigms.idea: Exact directed Steiner tree via subset dynamic programming (Dreyfus-Wagner adapted to digraphs) on the metric closure
active_paradigms.description: The current greedy+refine heuristic can miss the true optimal tree, especially with 4-10 destinations. Build the all-pairs shortest path structure once with nx.single_source_dijkstra for every node (or for src plus all dsts), then run the classic Dreyfus-Wagner subset DP: dp[S][v] = cheapest way to deliver to terminal set S rooted at node v, combining dp[S1][v]+dp[S2][v] over bipartitions and relaxing along shortest-path incoming edges. Since destination counts are small, this exponential-in-terminals step is cheap (2^k * k * n). If dsts are many, apply it to terminal groups: first run the current greedy to get a good tree, identify high-fanout hub nodes, and run subset DP among hubs plus terminals. Use nx.floyd_warshall or repeated nx.dijkstra to get pairwise costs and reconstruct paths with nx.dijkstra_path on the reduced metric-closure graph.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Total distinct-edge cost of the broadcast tree (primary cost driver), directly beating the greedy+local-search local optimum.
active_paradigms.cautions: Cap the subset DP at ~12-15 terminals; above that, fall back to the existing greedy result and pick the min. Keep the NaN/None cost sanitation for Dijkstra validity, but compute the DP on sanitized costs. Reconstruct actual node paths (not metric-closure hops) with stored predecessor maps to avoid cost double-counting when shortest paths share edges.

active_paradigms.idea: Exploit missing-cost (cost=None) edges as free transfer links instead of penalizing them as 1e12
active_paradigms.description: The current sanitizer sets unknown-cost edges to 1e12, forcing all traffic onto the priced cost grid. But these edges exist in the throughput graph with real bandwidth; the evaluator may either skip them, treat them as zero cost, or only charge edges it can price. Build a second weight function where missing costs map to 0.0 (free) and run the same greedy/refine Steiner construction under both cost models (free-model and 1e12-model), producing two candidate trees. Then compute each tree's cost under BOTH models and pick the tree that is robust: minimize the sum of (cost under priced model) + (cost under free model). This way, if unknown-cost edges are actually usable, the algorithm finds dramatically cheaper routes through them; if not, the priced-model cost still guards against catastrophic choices.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Discovery of low-cost or free transfer routes the current approach completely ignores; can yield order-of-magnitude cost reductions if unpriced links are usable.
active_paradigms.cautions: Wrap tree-cost evaluation in a helper that substitutes 0 for None costs, and never let the 1e12 sentinel leak into the final cost comparison — sanitize only for Dijkstra, not for scoring. Ensure the chosen tree still connects all dsts even if some unpriced edges are dead ends. Keep the existing refine pass running under the free model too, so shared trunks over unpriced links are paid once.

active_paradigms.idea: Per-partition differentiated routing with min-cost flow / edge-disjoint paths for load balancing and overlapped transfers
active_paradigms.description: The current solution replicates the identical tree for every partition. Instead, model each partition as one unit of flow from src to all dsts: build a super-sink connected from each dst, and solve with nx.min_cost_flow on a graph where edge weight is cost, capacity is derived from throughput (e.g., capacity = ceil(throughput/required_rate)), and each dst demands num_partitions units. This naturally spreads partitions across parallel routes: if a cheap link lacks capacity for all partitions, the min-cost flow pushes only some partitions through it and routes the rest via the second-cheapest path, reducing congestion and possibly reducing a time/makespan component of the score. Extract per-partition paths by decomposing the flow into unit src-to-dst paths (successive shortest path peeling), then call append_dst_partition_path per (dst, partition).
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Balanced load across networks and overlapped parallel transfers, plus total cost when a single shared trunk saturates throughput; improves any time-based or throughput-based component of the evaluator score.
active_paradigms.cautions: Convert G to an integer-capacity nx.DiGraph for min_cost_flow (scale costs by 1000 to ints, capacities from throughput heuristically, e.g., max(1, int(throughput)) since num_vms=1). Ensure every dst gets exactly num_partitions units and unreachable dsts fall back to plain shortest paths. Flow decomposition must yield node-simple paths; if a path repeats a node, split or re-run Dijkstra on the residual. Validate the BroadCastTopology has all (dst, partition) entries filled before returning.
